title: A regular ring is normal
statement: Let $R$ be a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] (Noetherian, with every localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ at a prime ideal a regular local ring). Then $R$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]: every $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a normal domain.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0567 (lemma-regular-normal, line 44046) and its proof: Serre's criterion Lemma Tag 031S (lemma-criterion-normal), a regular local ring is Cohen-Macaulay by Lemma Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM), giving (S_2); (R_1) is immediate

proof.text: *$(R_1)$.* By definition [def-weil-regular-scheme] a regular ring $R$ is Noetherian and $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a regular local ring for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$; in particular for every prime $\mathfrak p$ of height $\le1$. This is property $(R_1)$ of [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk] (1) with $k=1$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0567 (lemma-regular-normal, line 44046), proof: 'Property $(R_1)$ is immediate'; Definition Tag 00OD (definition-regular, line 27149), Definition Tag 031P (definition-conditions, line 43872)

proof.text: *$(S_2)$.* Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be a prime and $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A=\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ and $d=\dim A$ (the height of $\mathfrak p$). By [def-weil-regular-scheme] $A$ is a regular local ring, so $d$ is a non-negative integer and $\mathfrak m_A$ is generated by $d$ elements $x_1,\dots,x_d\in\mathfrak m_A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] $x_1,\dots,x_d$ is a regular sequence in $A$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and all $x_i$ lie in $\mathfrak m_A$. Since $\mathfrak m_A\cdot A=\mathfrak m_A\ne A$, the depth of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-depth] is the supremum of the lengths of regular sequences in $\mathfrak m_A$, hence $\operatorname{depth}(A)\ge d\ge\min\{2,d\}$ (for $d=0$ the empty sequence gives $\operatorname{depth}(A)\ge0$). As $\mathfrak p$ was arbitrary, $R$ has property $(S_2)$ of [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk] (2). (This is the 'regular local rings are Cohen-Macaulay' of the source, used only through the inequality $\operatorname{depth}\ge\dim$.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0567 (lemma-regular-normal, line 44046), proof: 'As a regular local ring is Cohen-Macaulay, see Lemma 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM, line 25732), it is clear that $R$ is $(S_2)$'; Definition Tag 00LI (definition-depth, line 17766)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (part of the definition of a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]) and has $(R_1)$ (step 1) and $(S_2)$ (step 2). By Serre's criterion [lem-weil-pbc-serre-criterion-normal], direction $(R_1)+(S_2)\Rightarrow$ normal, $R$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]: every $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a normal domain.
